$comment: Shared cross-VM golden vectors for the Eco intent chainer.
The EVM IntentChainer (eco/eco-routes) and the SVM intent-chainer
(eco/eco-routes-svm) owe each other agreement on the BYTES THEY PRODUCE, not
on the shape of the input that produces them. Nothing else in either suite
checks that. A transform mismatch, an endianness flip, or ceil landing on the
wrong side would each pass every same-side test and still disagree across the
boundary — and would surface in production as a solver delivering the wrong
This file is the fixture both suites assert against. Check the SAME file into
both repos. To add a vector, produce it on one side and confirm the other
where segments.length == slots.length + 1, and each slot writes amount_out
in its own width and byte order, reverting rather than truncating.

vectors.name: solana-lane-usdc-400bps-spread
description: The Solana lane as DepositAddress_USDCTransfer_Solana._encodeRoute emits it:
one token leg, one SPL transfer_checked call, four account metas. The amount
appears twice, both 8-byte little-endian u64, at offsets 116 and 169 for this
shape. Segments were cut from the route that production encoder emitted;
expected_route is what the EVM IntentChainer published for these inputs.
